elements.requirement: A court may only make a care order or supervision order if it is satisfied that the harm, or likelihood of harm, is attributable to the care given to the child, or likely to be given to him if the order were not made, not being what it would be reasonable to expect a parent to give to him, or to the child being beyond parental control.

elements.requirement: The permanence provisions of a section 31A plan include provisions setting out the long-term plan for the child's upbringing that provide for the child to live with any parent or other family member or friend, adoption, or other long-term care.

elements.requirement: The permanence provisions of a section 31A plan include provisions setting out the impact on the child of any harm suffered or likely to be suffered, the child's current and future needs (including needs arising from that impact), and how the long-term plan would meet those needs.
